headline: Maalaea Shoreline Home & Olowalu Ag Estate Reviewed

meeting.body: Maalaea Shoreline Home & Olowalu Ag Estate Reviewed
meeting.summary: The board backed roof and tree recommendations for a Māʻalaea home and recommended a community meeting on an Olowalu farm-home project.
meeting.recap: The Urban Design Review Board met July 7, 2026.[[0:00:30]] First up was a new home with a detached garage, ohana and pool on a Māʻalaea shoreline lot.[[0:01:10]] The chair listed two recommendations: consider a Class A fire-rated roof, and keep tree canopies from hanging over neighboring lots.[[0:54:20]] The recommendations passed with five votes in favor and one abstention.[[0:55:31]] The chair stepped aside from the second item because the chair's company consults on it.[[0:56:25]] The planner said it does not need a major SMA permit, partly because it is under 7,500 square feet.[[0:58:56]] Planning staff said the referral motion did not pass because only five members were voting.[[1:57:11]] The board voted to recommend a community meeting on the project.[[2:00:29]] Staff said a Lāhainā wildfire rebuild of a single-family home will come before the board.[[2:02:04]]
meeting.next: The Māʻalaea home's SMA permit will go before the Maui Planning Commission for public testimony at a future date. Staff said a Lāhainā wildfire rebuild of a single-family home will come before the board. Staff said a project with multifamily residences will also come before the board. Staff said board members will get training on their rules, duties and responsibilities.
